title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics + tracing, dashboard panels, and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into KV cache behavior at token granularity to understand tail-latency and per-token cost for production workloads. This PR introduces token-level KV cache metrics, tracing hooks for request->cache interactions, Grafana dashboard panels, and tuned alerts to reduce noisy SRE pages.

What I changed: - Added metrics for kv_cache.hit_count, kv_cache.miss_count, kv_cache.hit_latency_ms, kv_cache.kv_lookup_ops_per_token, and kv_cache.kv_memory_bytes (all labeled by model, deployment, route, and token_bucket).
- Instrumented critical code paths to emit a span for KV lookup lifecycle (kv.lookup.start / kv.lookup.end) including outcome and latency. Spans are correlated to request trace IDs so we can join traces and metrics.
- New Grafana dashboard JSON (observability/dashboards/token-kv-cache.json) with panels: token-level hit rate heatmap, per-deployment kv lookup latency histogram, cost-per-token breakdown combining model token cost and KV ops, and an anomaly panel for sudden drops in cache hit rate.
- Alert tuning: introduced two new alerts and adjusted thresholds on existing ones: KV_HIT_RATE_DROP (5m, p95 hit rate drop > 8%), KV_LOOKUP_LATENCY_TAIL (1m, p99 latency > 120ms), and reduced noisy pages by adding a suppression window during rolling deploys (using deployment label and rollout window).
- Tests: unit tests for metric emission, integration tests that validate trace->metric correlation, and a small local-dashboard preview script.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics emitted with correct labels and tag cardinality limits (bounded token_bucket buckets) - [x] Tracing spans created and include outcome & request_id - [x] Dashboard panels render with simulated data - [x] Alert rules include runbook links and SLO references - [x] Docs: observability/README updated with examples and migration notes

Notes on scope and limits: To avoid high cardinality, token-level metrics aggregate tokens into 10 fixed buckets (short/punct/long/token-position ranges); we validated offline with production traces to ensure stable cardinality. Memory accounting metric reports total KV memory usage per deployment to help capacity planning.

Related: ENG-2142 (observability token-level roadmap), SUP-8791 (customer-reported KV tail latencies).

release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics and tracing, new Grafana dashboard panels for KV cache (token-level hit rate heatmap, lookup latency histograms, cost-per-token breakdown), and tuned alerts to reduce noise while catching tail latency regressions.
notes: Follow-up items: (1) roll out dashboard to stable and canary orgs separately (ENG-2150), (2) propagate kv memory metric to capacity autoscaler (future PR), (3) consider exporting per-route sampled traces to long-term storage for offline flamegraphing.
risk_assessment: Low risk: metrics and tracing additions are additive and behind opt-in config for private deployments. Alert thresholds tuned conservatively to start.
